rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_unconstrained-claude-agentic: image_size=512, pixel_spacing=0.3516, n_angles=128, n_det=1024, det_spacing=0.35754, sod=500.0, sdd=1000.0, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.5, train_n=400, val_n=200, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_breast.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.01, fd_recon_eta=0.1, fd_recon_dc=0, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.5, rationale=iter-15: DC-off breast-prior. ONE KNOB init_t 0.02->0.01. BREAKTHROUGH at iter-14: init_t0.02 gave hr=0.2085 (PSNR38.36 > FBP baseline 36.32; RMSE4.13e-3 < baseline 5.21e-3) - the breast prior CLEARED the baseline! MECHANISM: at init_t~0.02 the FBP is embedded at ~2% noise and the prior acts as a learned FBP-DENOISER (well-conditioned 128-view breast: FBP has removable noise; the prior's light denoise + whisper of DPS drops RMSE below raw FBP). So the DC-off prior DOES contribute (21% headroom recovered) as a denoiser, NOT just recovering FBP. HYPOTHESIS: init_t=0.01 - is hr still rising (even lighter touch) or did the peak pass at 0.02? Brackets the hr peak. Also a robustness check that iter-14's cross was not a fluke.
